title: Pack the Pantry enters its final week — Community Day set for Saturday at Pla-Mor
excerpt: The TAMIU Alumni Association's Pack the Pantry donation drive enters its final week, with donations accepted through Friday, Nov. 14, and a Community Day celebration set for Saturday, Nov. 14, from 2 to 6 p.m. at Pla-Mor Entertainment, 2819 Bob Bullock Loop.
content:
The TAMIU Alumni Association's Pack the Pantry donation drive enters its final week, with donations accepted through Friday, Nov. 14, and a Community Day celebration set for Saturday, Nov. 14, from 2 to 6 p.m. at Pla-Mor Entertainment, 2819 Bob Bullock Loop.

The drive, called “Dustdevils Helping Dustdevils,” stocks Dusty's Food Pantry, the on-campus pantry that provides food and everyday essentials to Texas A&M International University students facing food insecurity and basic-needs challenges. It launched Oct. 19 and brings together alumni, students, local businesses and community organizations.

“Pack the Pantry represents the spirit of giving back and supporting the next generation of Dustdevils. Together, we can make a meaningful difference in the lives of our students,” said David “Kash” Vasquez, president of the TAMIU Alumni Association.

Twelve drop-off sites across Laredo are accepting donations: the TAMIU Office of Student Affairs (Student Center, Room 226) and the Office of Alumni Relations (Killam Library, Room 261), both at 5201 University Blvd.; the Fernando A. Salinas Community Center, 520 Reynolds St.; the Fred M. and Anita Bruni Community Center, 452 Ranch Penitas Rd.; Jet Bowl North, 5823 McPherson Road; Laredo Title and Abstract, 415 Shiloh Dr.; the Lilia Perez Community Center, 4420 Old Santa María Rd.; the Lollipop Learning Center, 1701 Peaceful Meadow Ct.; Pla-Mor Entertainment, 2819 Bob Bullock Loop; the Sames Auto Arena, 6700 Arena Blvd.; the Webb County Treasurer's Office, 1110 Washington St., Suite 202; and 550 Pizzeria, 2101 Shiloh Dr.

Most-needed items are nonperishable foods — canned proteins, canned fruits and vegetables, rice, pasta, cereal, peanut butter and shelf-stable milk — plus personal hygiene products such as toothpaste, shampoo, deodorant, soap and feminine hygiene products. Donors can also give diapers, baby wipes and infant formula.

“Having access to basic necessities allows students to focus on their education and well-being. We are grateful to the Alumni Association and community partners for their continued support,” said Melissa D. Olivarez, a program specialist in the TAMIU Office of Student Affairs and foster care liaison.

Students can also earn community service hours through the drive — one hour for every five qualifying food items or three qualifying hygiene products donated, up to the university's 10-hour monthly maximum. Recognized student organizations are competing in a friendly contest to see which group collects the most. “A little friendly competition can go a long way when it's for a great cause,” said Rebecca “Christy” Rangel-Bryand, secretary of the Alumni Association.

Saturday's Community Day is the finale. “We want Pack the Pantry Community Day to be more than just a donation drive,” said Jorge Luis Quijano, past president of the Alumni Association and chair of the initiative. “It's an opportunity for families, alumni and students to come together, enjoy an afternoon at Pla-Mor and give back to our Dustdevil community.” For more information, contact the TAMIU Alumni Association at alumni@tamiu.edu. Webb Watch covered the launch of the drive on Oct. 21.
